claims.claim: Timepoints 30 s, 2,880 per day; interactive smoothed 5 to 64 minutes; background 24 hours; F2 1 CU hour example ~2.1%; throttling stages at 10 min, 60 min, 24 h with 20 s interactive delay.
Surge protection: capacity-level background rejection threshold; workspace-level CU cap over rolling 24 h with Mission Critical exclusion.
Capacity Metrics app installed by capacity admin; Health page; Compute page 14-day view.

concept_html:
Every Fabric operation draws capacity units (CUs) from its workspace's capacity (lesson C1-L1). Fabric lets operations burst above the capacity's size, then smooths the cost over future time (Microsoft Learn, checked September 2026).

Smoothing. Fabric measures usage in 30-second timepoints, 2,880 per day.

  • Interactive operations, such as report queries, are smoothed over at least 5 minutes and up to 64 minutes.
  • Background operations, such as scheduled Spark jobs, pipeline runs and model refreshes, are smoothed over 24 hours.

Example: an F2 has 2 CUs, or 48 CU hours per day. A background job that uses 1 CU hour adds 1 / 48, about 2.1%, to every timepoint for the next 24 hours.

Throttling starts when smoothed usage borrows too much future capacity:

Future capacity already used What happens
Up to 10 minutes Overage protection: no throttling
Over 10, up to 60 minutes Interactive jobs are delayed by 20 seconds
Over 60 minutes, up to 24 hours Interactive jobs are rejected
Over 24 hours All requests are rejected, background too

Background jobs keep running well after users feel the delay. A capacity deep in debt takes hours to recover, because only idle capacity pays it back.

Surge protection lets capacity admins reject background jobs earlier, before the capacity reaches deep throttling. At workspace level, it caps a workspace's share of CU use over a rolling 24 hours, unless you tag the workspace Mission Critical.

The Capacity Metrics app shows what happened. A capacity admin installs it and shares it. The Health page flags throttling and rejections across your capacities. The Compute page gives 14 days of utilisation by item and operation.

Practical rules: schedule heavy background jobs away from business hours, keep production on its own capacity, and check the Compute page before you buy a larger SKU.

exercises.prompt: Write `throttle_stage(future_minutes: float) -> str` returning the throttling stage for minutes of future capacity already used: `"none"` up to 10, `"interactive_delay"` above 10 up to 60, `"interactive_rejection"` above 60 up to 1,440 (24 hours), and `"background_rejection"` above that. Raise `ValueError` for negative input. Keep the limits in constants.
exercises.prompt_html: Write throttle_stage(future_minutes: float) -> str returning the throttling stage for minutes of future capacity already used: "none" up to 10, "interactive_delay" above 10 up to 60, "interactive_rejection" above 60 up to 1,440 (24 hours), and "background_rejection" above that. Raise ValueError for negative input. Keep the limits in constants.
exercises.solution:
OVERAGE_PROTECTION_MINUTES = 10
INTERACTIVE_DELAY_MINUTES = 60
INTERACTIVE_REJECTION_MINUTES = 24 * 60


def throttle_stage(future_minutes: float) -> str:
    """Fabric throttling stage for the future capacity already consumed.

    Args:
        future_minutes: Minutes of future capacity used by smoothed operations.

    Returns:
        "none", "interactive_delay", "interactive_rejection" or "background_rejection".

    Raises:
        ValueError: If future_minutes is negative.
    """
    if future_minutes < 0:
        raise ValueError("future_minutes must not be negative")
    if future_minutes <= OVERAGE_PROTECTION_MINUTES:
        return "none"
    if future_minutes <= INTERACTIVE_DELAY_MINUTES:
        return "interactive_delay"
    if future_minutes <= INTERACTIVE_REJECTION_MINUTES:
        return "interactive_rejection"
    return "background_rejection"

title: Capacity, smoothing and throttling
why_html: A team scheduled a full rebuild of 40 gold tables at 08:00 on an F16. By 09:30 the capacity had borrowed more than an hour of future use, and Power BI reports started failing for every user. The rebuild itself kept running. Moving it to 02:00, and making it incremental, kept the morning reports responsive without a larger SKU.
